questions.question: A company netting pilchards out of Saldanha Bay operates in which sector?
A software developer in Stellenbosch writes banking apps and never produces a physical object. The sector is:
options: Tertiary, because a service is being produced
None — only physical goods count as production

questions.question: Ranked by contribution to South Africa's GDP today, largest first, the sectors run:
Agriculture supplies only about 3% of GDP yet is described as large in livelihoods because:
options: Farm output is deliberately left out of GDP
Farmers earn more than bankers on average
Its share of employment, especially in rural districts with no other employers, far exceeds its share of GDP

subtopics.title: How the Sectors Link and How the Structure Has Shifted

questions.question: Rooibos grown in the Cederberg, packed at a processing plant, and sold by a supermarket passes through the sectors in the order:
The ordered journey of an economy's weight from primary to secondary to tertiary is called:
Since the early 1990s, manufacturing's share of South Africa's GDP has:
Premature deindustrialisation worries economists in South Africa specifically because:
options: Factories emit more carbon than offices
Manufacturing is the great absorber of semi-skilled labour, which an economy with unemployment above 30% desperately needs

questions.question: Which of the following is SOCIAL rather than economic infrastructure?
options: A bulk water pipeline to a factory zone

questions.question: According to the lesson, a hospital raises national output:
options: Indirectly — treated workers return to the economy more productive
Not at all — health spending is pure consumption
Only through the wages it pays nurses

questions.question: A failure of shared infrastructure is compared to a tax because it:
options: Raises costs for producers in all three sectors at the same moment

questions.question: Mineral exporters recently lost foreign buyers mainly because:
options: Locomotives, lines and port cranes could not shift the tonnage

subtopics.title: Service Provisioning, Access and Economic Opportunity

questions.question: Roughly what share of South African households has an electricity connection?
The remaining service-access gaps cluster mainly in:
options: Rural districts of the former homelands and informal settlements on metro edges

questions.question: South Africa's 'digital divide' chiefly describes:
options: Slow satellite internet on farms only
The poorest users paying the most, relative to income, for mobile data — or staying offline altogether

questions.question: The lesson's core mechanism is that weak service access:
options: Lowers the prices the poor pay for goods
Raises the price of participating in the economy, most steeply for the poor

subtopics.title: From the Ground, Through the Factory, Over the Counter

questions.question: The plant that ferments, dries and packs rooibos leaves into teabags belongs to which sector?
Of every R100 South Africa produces, services contribute roughly:
The lesson corrects a common belief by describing South Africa as:
options: A mining economy with some shops attached
A farming economy with famous banks
A factory economy that closed its mines
A services economy that happens to own famous mines

subtopics.title: One Street, All Three Sectors Holding Hands

questions.question: If foot-and-mouth disease closes the cattle auctions, the boerewors-roll seller eventually feels it because:
options: Trouble at one station of the chain rides the line to the end

questions.question: Which ordering of eras matches South Africa's economic history?
options: Services era, factory decades, mines-and-farms era
Factory decades, mines-and-farms era, services era
Mines-and-farms era, factory decades, services era

questions.question: Factory jobs are described as a particular loss for South Africa because they:
options: Fit workers who bring skill and effort but no university degree — the workers this economy has most of
Paid better than any service job
Could never be threatened by imports

subtopics.title: The Wires and Pipes That Decide Who Gets to Play

questions.question: During the power cut on the trading corner, every business suffered at once because:
options: The owners all took the afternoon off
One shared infrastructure failure stopped clippers, fridges, screens and card machines in the same minute

questions.question: Economists call repairing power, rail and ports the cheapest growth plan because:
options: Mending one shared thing lowers costs for thousands of businesses simultaneously
It removes the need for skills training

questions.question: A vacancy thirty kilometres away can be worthless to a poor job-seeker because:
options: Taxi fare can swallow so much of the wage that working produces almost nothing
